question: In which year did India win its first Olympic gold medal in hockey?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• India won its first-ever **Olympic gold medal** in hockey at the **1928 Amsterdam Olympics**. This victory marked the beginning of an era of unprecedented dominance for India in the sport of field hockey on the global stage.

• The Indian team was led by captain **Jaipal Singh Munda**, who was a prominent **Adivasi** leader and scholar. Under his leadership, the team displayed exceptional skill and coordination throughout the tournament.

• The legendary **Major Dhyan Chand**, often referred to as the **Wizard of Hockey**, emerged as the star performer of the **1928 Games**. He was the top scorer of the tournament, netting a total of **14 goals** in just five matches.

• In the final match held on **May 26, 1928**, India faced the host nation, the **Netherlands**. India secured a convincing **3-0** victory to claim the gold medal. Remarkably, the Indian team did not concede a single goal throughout the entire **1928 Olympic** tournament.

• The other options provided are significant but do not represent the first win: **1932** (Los Angeles) was India's second gold medal; **1948** (London) was the first gold medal won by India as an **independent nation**; and **1952** (Helsinki) was India's fifth consecutive gold medal.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Dominance in Olympics**: Following the **1928** win, India went on to win a record **six consecutive gold medals** in Olympic hockey from **1928 to 1956**. This remains one of the most impressive winning streaks in any team sport in Olympic history.

• **1932 Los Angeles Olympics**: India defended its title with a massive **24-1** victory over the **United States** in the final. This match remains famous for the highest number of goals scored in an international hockey match.

• **1936 Berlin Olympics**: India won its third consecutive gold by defeating **Germany** **8-1** in the final. This tournament solidified **Major Dhyan Chand's** reputation as the greatest hockey player of all time.

• **1948 London Olympics**: This was a historic moment as India defeated **Great Britain** **4-0** in the final at **Wembley Stadium**. It was the first time the **Indian National Anthem** was played and the **Tricolour** was hoisted at the Olympics after independence.

• **1980 Moscow Olympics**: India won its **eighth gold medal** in hockey at the **Moscow Games**, captained by **Vasudevan Baskaran**. This was the last gold medal for India in hockey for several decades.

• **Recent Achievements**: After a gap of **41 years**, the Indian men's hockey team won a **bronze medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** (held in **2021**) and followed it up with another **bronze medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.

**Important Points__**

• **Indian Hockey Federation (IHF)**: The governing body for hockey in India was formed in **1925** in **Gwalior**. It was the first non-European hockey federation to be admitted to the **International Hockey Federation (FIH)**.

• **National Sports Day**: In honor of **Major Dhyan Chand's** contributions to the sport, his birthday, **August 29**, is celebrated as **National Sports Day** in India every year.

• **Balbir Singh Sr.**: Another legendary figure in Indian hockey, he was part of the gold-winning teams in **1948**, **1952**, and **1956**. He holds the record for the most goals scored by an individual in an Olympic men's hockey final, scoring **5 goals** against the **Netherlands** in **1952**.

• **Total Olympic Medals**: As of **2024**, India has won a total of **13 Olympic medals** in hockey, consisting of **8 gold**, **1 silver**, and **4 bronze** medals.
